passive_skill.name: Enlightened Presence
passive_skill.description: Shenlong's very existence radiates peace and wisdom. Allies near him gradually recover from mental effects, have their spiritual cultivation enhanced, and feel their doubts and fears dissolve. Enemies near him find their bloodlust cooling, their hatred fading, and have difficulty committing to violent acts. His silver aura also reveals hidden truths, making invisible enemies visible and exposing deception.

special_skills.name: Wisdom's Gaze
special_skills.description: Shenlong touches his right index ring, and his silver-blue eyes flash with golden light. For a short time, he can see the true nature of all beings and situations—enemy weaknesses are revealed, illusions are pierced, and the best path forward becomes clear. Allies near him also gain increased accuracy and critical chance as he guides them.

special_skills.name: Protection's Shield
special_skills.description: He raises his left hand, and the shield ring blazes with silver light. A dome of protective energy expands around himself and his chosen allies, absorbing all incoming damage for a duration. The dome also reflects a portion of the damage back at attackers as pure enlightenment, calming their violent intentions.

special_skills.name: Diligence's Flame
special_skills.description: Shenlong touches his right ring finger, and his entire form becomes wreathed in soft silver flames. For a duration, his attacks are faster, his movements quicker, and each strike carries the focused intensity of enlightenment, dealing bonus damage and leaving targets momentarily enlightened (reducing their desire to fight).

special_skills.name: Healing's Bloom
special_skills.description: He spreads both hands, and flowering branches of silver light extend from his healing ring, touching all allies in range. Wounds close, illnesses fade, and even spiritual damage is mended. The healing continues for a short time after the initial touch.

ultimate_skill.name: Enlightened Fist: Ten-Ring Harmony
ultimate_skill.description: Shenlong Xu closes his eyes and brings his hands together, palm to palm, the ten silver rings aligning in perfect harmony. For a single breath, all is still. Then his eyes open, blazing with silver-gold light, and all ten rings activate simultaneously. From his right hand: compassion, wisdom, patience, diligence, and peace flow outward in waves of silver light. From his left hand: strength, protection, healing, clarity, and transcendence join the harmony. The ten powers intertwine, forming a living mandala of light that expands to cover the entire battlefield. For the duration of the ultimate, Shenlong becomes the embodiment of enlightenment—he moves with impossible grace, each gesture a prayer, each step a blessing. Enemies find their violence neutralized, their hatred dissolved, their darkness lifted—not through force, but through the overwhelming power of peace. Allies feel their spirits elevated, their wounds healed, their doubts erased. And Shenlong himself floats at the center of it all, his long silver hair flowing like a river of light, his ethereal face serene, his ten rings blazing with the combined power of a thousand enlightened masters. When the ultimate ends, the light fades slowly, and Shenlong descends gently to the ground, his rings dimming to their usual soft glow. He looks at those around him, his silver-blue eyes holding only compassion, and speaks one word: 'Peace.' He is Shenlong Xu, the Enlightened Fist, and he has shown the world what true power looks like.

title: The First Vampire
nickname: Crimson Crow of the Eternal Night
lore: Before the first vampire clans, before the bloodlines and the covens, before the legends that would terrify generations, there was Valogueneir Kimpatsu. He was not born of darkness—he was driven into it. In an age when kingdoms rose and fell on the whims of nobles, Valogueneir was a young lord of exceptional beauty and gentle heart, married to his beloved wife Amara and father to their infant son Lysander. Their household was modest but happy, until the day the king's advisors cast envious eyes upon their lands. False charges were brought, accusations of treason and dark magic, and in a single night, soldiers descended upon their manor. Valogueneir was away, negotiating trade agreements in a distant city. He returned to find his wife violated and murdered, his son's broken body in the garden, and his home reduced to ash. His screams echoed through the valley, reaching the ears of an ancient being that dwelt in the depths of the world—the first vampire, a creature of such power that it had slumbered since before humanity's dawn. It offered Valogueneir a choice: die in grief, or become something new, something that could never be hurt again, something that would make the kings of men tremble. Valogueneir accepted. He drank the ancient blood and rose as the first of a new kind—a vampire who feared no light, thirsted not for human blood, and could take the form of a crow rather than a bat. Now, after centuries of existence, he hunts not men, but the demons that whisper cruelty into human hearts. He is Valogueneir Kimpatsu, the Crimson Crow, the First Vampire, and his amber hair and ruby eyes hide a grief as deep as eternity.
description: Valogueneir Kimpatsu is the embodiment of tragic, aristocratic beauty—a vampire whose centuries of existence have only refined his features into something almost unbearably lovely. He stands in the ruined garden where his family died, his tall slender form silhouetted against the full moon, his magnificent long amber permed hair cascading past his shoulders in soft voluminous waves that catch the moonlight like spun gold touched by sunset, each perfect curl moving slightly in the night breeze, inviting the touch. His body is tall and slender with the graceful build of aristocracy—long limbs, elegant posture, and a presence that commands attention without effort. His chest is visible through the open front of his elaborate robes, revealing smooth pale skin with a faint rosy undertone and the subtle definition of lean muscle beneath. His face is a perfect oval with soft features that give him an almost cute appearance despite his ancient nature—high cheekbones that catch light, a gentle jawline that speaks of kindness rather than severity, and a small delicate chin, all combining to create a face of such flawless beauty that it inspires both awe and protectiveness in those who behold it. His large almond-shaped ruby red eyes sparkle like cut gems, holding both the warmth of the loving husband he once was and the cold eternity of what he has become, tears of crimson light not quite falling from their corners. The elaborate royal vampire robes of deepest crimson and black velvet flow around him, the silver and gold embroidery of crows in flight and crescent moons catching the moonlight, and the multiple gold chains at his neck with their ruby and onyx settings gleam against the white silk of his ruffled shirt. The robes are open at the chest, revealing the smooth expanse of his pale skin and the delicate lines of his collarbones. At his shoulders, the gold crow-head clasps with their ruby eyes seem to watch the graves with him, and on his slender fingers, the numerous rings—the large signet ring with his lost house crest, the ruby ring on his left index, the golden bands—catch light and throw it back in tiny reflections. Around him, hundreds of crows perch in absolute silence on every ruined wall, every branch, every surface, their ruby eyes reflecting the moonlight, watching over their master and the graves he will never abandon. He does not move, does not speak, simply stands in eternal vigil, his form occasionally dissolving at the edges into a swirl of black feathers before reforming, as if even his physical presence cannot decide whether to stay or to join them in death. Those who have glimpsed him speak of a grief so profound that it becomes a physical presence, a weight in the air that makes breathing difficult, a sorrow so deep that it threatens to drown anyone who comes too close. They also speak of his devastating beauty, the way the moonlight catches his amber curls and ruby eyes, the way his pale skin seems to glow, the way his grief only makes him more achingly beautiful. He is often found in this garden, at this grave, beneath this tree, but sometimes he walks the world, hunting the demons that whisper cruelty into human hearts, his crows his only companions, his ruby eyes the last thing many evil beings ever see. He is Valogueneir Kimpatsu, the First Vampire, and his love for his lost family is the only light in his immortal darkness.

story.part1: Valogueneir Kimpatsu was born the second son of a minor noble house in a kingdom whose name has long been forgotten. His elder brother inherited the lands and titles, leaving Valogueneir with a small manor, a few fields, and the freedom to pursue his own path. He chose love. At a festival celebrating the harvest, he met Amara, a merchant's daughter with laughter like wind chimes and eyes that held the warmth of a thousand suns. They married within the year, and when their son Lysander was born, Valogueneir held the infant in his arms and wept with joy. Those were the happiest years of his life—simple, peaceful, perfect. He had no ambition for power or wealth; he had everything he needed within the walls of his modest home.
story.part2: The king's advisor, a man named Mordred whose cruelty was matched only by his greed, had long coveted the fertile lands that bordered Valogueneir's manor. He fabricated evidence of treason, claimed that Valogueneir was plotting with neighboring kingdoms, and convinced the aging king to sign a warrant for the household's execution. Valogueneir, oblivious to the danger, had traveled to the capital to negotiate a trade agreement that would benefit his tenants. He was three days away when Mordred's soldiers descended upon his home.
story.part3: He returned on the fourth day, riding through the gates with gifts for his wife and son. The gates hung broken. The house was ash. And in the garden, beneath the tree where Lysander had taken his first steps, he found them. Amara's body bore the marks of unspeakable violence. Little Lysander, barely two years old, had been thrown against the wall, his small form crumpled like discarded cloth. Valogueneir fell to his knees and screamed until his voice gave out, then screamed in silence until the stars wheeled overhead and dawn began to break. He did not know how long he knelt there, but when he finally rose, something inside him had died—and something else had awakened.
story.part4: He carried their bodies to the crypt behind the ruined manor and buried them with his own hands, speaking words of love and grief and a promise: 'I will find those who did this. I will make them understand what they have taken. And when I am done, there will be no trace of them left in this world.' He walked into the mountains, into the caves where no man had ventured, seeking the ancient power that legend said dwelled in the darkness. For seven days he descended, through caverns of crystal and tunnels of obsidian, until he reached the heart of the world. There, in a chamber of absolute black, he found it—the First Vampire, a being of such ancient power that it had slept since before humanity's first cities. It spoke in his mind: 'I know why you have come. I know your grief, your rage, your hunger for justice. I offer you a choice: die here, alone, and join your family in death, or drink of my blood and become something new. You will walk in sunlight, for I have conquered it. You will thirst not for human blood, for that is a lesser hunger. You will become a hunter of the darkness that lurks in human hearts, the demonic whispers that drive men to cruelty. Choose.' Valogueneir chose.
story.part5: He drank, and the transformation was agony beyond anything he had imagined—every cell of his body died and was reborn, his blood turned to liquid fire, his heart stopped and started again with a new rhythm. When it was over, he rose as the first of his kind. He found that he could transform into a crow, his consciousness spreading into the flock of birds that had gathered in the cavern. He found that sunlight did not burn him, for the ancient vampire's blood had conquered that weakness. He found that human blood held no appeal—his hunger was for something deeper, the demonic essence that corrupted human hearts and drove them to evil. He emerged from the mountain a new being, and he began his hunt.
story.part6: Mordred died first, a year after the transformation. Valogueneir spent months learning his habits, his defenses, his fears. He appeared to Mordred in dreams as a crow with ruby eyes, drove him slowly mad with anticipation. When he finally struck, it was in the king's own court, in front of all the nobles who had laughed at Mordred's jokes. He descended from the rafters in a whirlwind of black feathers, took human form for just a moment—long enough for Mordred to see the face of the man he had wronged—and then drained not his blood, but the demonic essence that had corrupted his soul. Mordred did not die; he simply became... empty, a hollow shell with no will, no cruelty, no nothing. He spent the rest of his life as a drooling simpleton, and Valogueneir considered that justice enough.
story.part7: Now, centuries later, Valogueneir Kimpatsu walks the world as a legend whispered among those who know of the supernatural. He is known as the First Vampire, the Crimson Crow, the Lord of the Eternal Night. His appearance is that of a young man in his mid-twenties, impossibly handsome with a flawless, almost cute face that belies the ancient grief within. His amber hair, long and beautifully permed, cascades in soft waves past his shoulders, catching light like spun gold touched by sunset. His eyes sparkle like cut rubies, deep crimson with flecks of diamond light, holding both the warmth of the man he once was and the cold eternity of what he has become. He dresses like the king he might have been—elaborate robes of deepest crimson and black, embroidered with silver and gold thread in patterns of crows and moonlight, layered with velvet and silk, adorned with countless ornaments: rings on every finger, chains of precious metal, a signet ring bearing the crest of his lost house, a brooch in the shape of a crow in flight. He carries no weapon, for he needs none—his hands, his eyes, his very presence are weapons enough. He hunts now not for revenge, but for purpose, seeking out the demonic influences that corrupt humanity and draining them from their hosts, leaving behind people who can choose good or evil for themselves. He is immune to sunlight, free of the thirst for human blood, and forever bound to the grief that made him. He is Valogueneir Kimpatsu, the First Vampire, and he watches over humanity from the shadows, a guardian born of tragedy, a king without a kingdom, a crow forever circling the memories of what he lost.

The robes are open at the chest, revealing the smooth pale skin and the subtle definition of his pectorals.
upper_body.shoulders: Graceful and straight, draped in the heavy fabric of his outer robe which is fastened at the shoulders with ornate gold clasps shaped like crow heads with ruby eyes
upper_body.neck: Long and elegant, adorned with multiple gold chains of varying lengths, some set with small rubies, others with black onyx, the longest chain bearing a pendant of a crow with spread wings crafted from blackened silver
upper_body.waist: Narrow, cinched by a wide belt of black leather overlaid with gold scales, from which hang various ornamental chains and a small velvet pouch

lower_body.hips: Narrow and graceful
lower_body.legs: Long and elegant, clad in tight black silk trousers that disappear into his boots, the fabric rich and smooth, hinting at the lean muscles beneath
lower_body.feet: Clad in tall black leather boots with gold trim and small heels, the boots polished to a mirror shine, embroidered with gold thread in patterns of crow feathers along the sides

clothing.head: His magnificent long amber permed hair cascading past his shoulders in soft waves; small gold crow-feather earrings at his ears
clothing.upper: Layered royal robes of deepest crimson and black velvet over a white silk shirt with ruffled collar—the inner robe of crimson silk embroidered with gold thread, the outer robe of black velvet embroidered with silver crows and moons, fastened at shoulders with gold crow-head clasps set with ruby eyes; the robes are strategically open at the chest, revealing the smooth pale skin beneath; numerous gold chains at his neck of varying lengths with ruby and onyx settings, the longest bearing a blackened silver crow pendant
clothing.lower: Tight black silk trousers disappearing into tall black leather boots with gold trim and small heels, the boots embroidered with gold crow-feather patterns
clothing.accessories: Multiple rings on his slender fingers—a large signet ring with his lost house crest on right hand, a ruby ring on left index, several golden bands; gold chains at neck with ruby and onyx; blackened silver crow pendant; gold crow-head clasps at shoulders; gold earrings shaped like crow feathers; a wide black leather belt with gold scales at his waist; a small velvet pouch hanging from his belt containing mementos of his wife and son

weapon.name: Sanguine Crown (His Vampiric Powers)
weapon.type: Innate Abilities Channeled Through His Body
weapon.aura: Soft crimson light tinged with gold that pulses gently around him, occasionally shifting to deep purple-black when he draws on his darker powers, with tiny sparkles of light that resemble distant stars or the glitter of rubies
weapon.special_feature: Valogueneir carries no physical weapon—his body and his ancient powers are weapon enough. His primary abilities manifest through his hands, his eyes, and his transformation. When he fights, his hands can extend into shadowy claws that drain demonic essence, his ruby eyes can freeze enemies with a glance, and his body can dissolve into a flock of crows at will. The Sanguine Crown is not a single power but the sum of all his vampiric abilities, each one refined over centuries of existence. He can summon crows from miles around to do his bidding, see through their eyes, and use them as extensions of his will. His ruby eyes can perceive the demonic corruption in any being, seeing it as dark tendrils within the soul. His touch can drain that corruption, leaving the host purified but exhausted. In combat, he moves with supernatural grace, each gesture a perfect economy of motion, his hands leaving trails of crimson light. When he transforms into a crow, he becomes a single bird or a flock, able to pass through the smallest openings, to observe without being observed, to strike from unexpected directions. And when he unleashes his full power, his form becomes a whirlwind of feathers and crimson light, a manifestation of grief and vengeance that terrifies even demons.

basic_skills.name: Crow Strike
basic_skills.description: Valogueneir extends his hand, and a crow made of shadow and crimson light shoots forward to strike an enemy. The crow deals damage and leaves a mark that allows him to track the target.

basic_skills.name: Ruby Gaze
basic_skills.description: His eyes flash with deep crimson light, locking onto a single enemy. The target is briefly paralyzed by the intensity of his gaze, unable to move or attack for a moment.

basic_skills.name: Feather Step
basic_skills.description: He dissolves into a swirl of crow feathers and reappears at a nearby location, untargetable during the movement and leaving behind a momentary distraction.

passive_skill.name: Eternal Grief
passive_skill.description: Valogueneir carries the weight of his lost family always. His presence evokes a profound sadness in those who behold him, making enemies hesitate before striking and reducing their combat effectiveness. Allies near him feel protected, as if his ancient sorrow creates a barrier against harm. Additionally, he can sense the location of any being with strong demonic corruption within a large radius.

special_skills.name: Crow Storm
special_skills.description: Valogueneir's form explodes into a swirling storm of crows—hundreds of them, each one a piece of his consciousness. The crows fill a large area, attacking enemies continuously, obscuring vision, and carrying his essence to any point within the storm. He can reform anywhere among the flock.

special_skills.name: Essence Drain
special_skills.description: He reaches out and touches an enemy, his hand becoming shadowy and insubstantial. He drains the demonic essence from them, dealing massive damage to corrupted beings and healing himself for a portion. Against pure enemies, the effect is less damaging but still leaves them weakened.

special_skills.name: Shadow Claws
special_skills.description: His hands transform into shadowy claws wreathed in crimson light. For a duration, his melee attacks deal bonus damage, ignore armor, and drain a small amount of essence with each strike, healing him over time.

special_skills.name: Crow's Memory
special_skills.description: Valogueneir closes his eyes and reaches out to every crow within miles. He can see through their eyes, hear through their ears, and move his consciousness between them. This grants him and his allies perfect vision of a huge area and reveals all hidden enemies.

ultimate_skill.name: First Vampire: Elegy of the Lost
ultimate_skill.description: Valogueneir's ruby eyes blaze with such intense crimson light that they seem to bleed fire. His amber hair rises as if caught in an ethereal wind, each perfect curl streaming behind him. His form dissolves not into crows, but into pure memory—the memory of his wife's laughter, his son's first steps, the warmth of his home before the flames. For the duration of the ultimate, the battlefield becomes saturated with his grief, and every enemy feels the weight of what was taken from him. Demonic beings are particularly affected, their corruption burning away under the intensity of pure, human sorrow. He moves through the battlefield as both man and memory, each touch not harming but overwhelming—enemies find themselves weeping, dropping their weapons, turning on each other as the grief becomes too much to bear. Crows fill the sky, their calls forming a mournful elegy that echoes across the battlefield. When the ultimate ends, Valogueneir reforms at the center, his eyes dimmer, his expression one of profound exhaustion mixed with something like peace. He has shared his burden, if only for a moment, and the world is a little lighter for it. He is Valogueneir Kimpatsu, the First Vampire, and his grief is both his curse and his greatest power.

title: The Crimson & Verdant Hunter
lore: In the mist-shrouded valleys of the eastern frontier, where ancient forests give way to abandoned temples and the howl of demons echoes through the night, a child was found in a basket floating down a river of blood. That child was Jasper Cole, and the only clue to his origin was a small pendant bearing the symbol of a holly leaf intertwined with a hawk's feather. He was raised by a reclusive demon hunter named Old Man Whitley, who trained him in the ancient arts of hunting the creatures that prey upon humanity. But Jasper was special—not just in his talent, which was considerable, but in his appearance. Even as he grew into a young man, his face retained the soft, rounded features of a boy, with cheeks that dimpled when he smiled and eyes that sparkled with an almost mischievous innocence. Enemies who saw him coming laughed at the child with the shotgun and sword. They stopped laughing when the holy water plasma burned through their demonic flesh. Now in his early twenties, Jasper Cole is known among the supernatural community as the Hollyhawk—a name that strikes fear into the hearts of demons and brings hope to the innocent. His red and green attire marks him like a walking Christmas card, a ironic contrast to the death he brings, and his unique scarf and hat have become legendary among those who hunt the darkness. He is the most unlikely demon hunter in existence, and perhaps the most effective.
description: Jasper Cole is a vision of boyish charm and lethal grace—a young man whose disarmingly cute appearance and lean athletic build create an irresistible combination that has lured countless demons to their doom. He strolls through the misty streets of the frontier town like he hasn't a care in the world, his hands in his pockets, his head tilted back to watch the stars through the fog, a young man so disarmingly cute that passing mothers smile at him and children wave without fear. His face is the kind that artists struggle to paint—not because it's complex, but because its simple, boyish perfection seems almost impossible to capture, with those rounded cheeks that dimple when he grins, that small straight nose, those large sparkling eyes of deep emerald green that hold a perpetual twinkle of mischief and warmth. His body is lean and athletic, built for speed and agility rather than brute strength, with the wiry musculature of someone who has trained in combat since childhood—not bulky, but every muscle defined and efficient. His chest is visible through the open front of his crimson coat, revealing the lean, defined planes of his pectorals and the subtle ridges of his abdominal muscles. His shoulders are straight and well-proportioned, his arms lean but corded with muscle, and his waist is narrow and flexible. His skin is fair with a warm undertone, lightly freckled across the nose and cheeks from years of outdoor hunting, the freckles adding to his boyish charm. His rich chestnut brown hair is cut in a practical but stylish manner, with a few deliberate strands always falling across his forehead no matter how often he pushes them back, giving him that perpetually slightly disheveled look that adds to his charm. But it is his attire that makes him unforgettable—a long coat of deep crimson red, tailored perfectly to his lean athletic frame, with verdant green embroidery along the lapels and cuffs in patterns of holly leaves and thorns, the coat falling to his knees and parting to reveal a green waistcoat beneath with matching red embroidery and the tantalizing glimpse of his lean torso. Around his neck, wrapped with casual elegance, is his signature scarf—a masterpiece of red and green fabric woven with silver threads that seem to glow faintly in darkness, the scarf long enough to wrap twice and still trail behind him in the wind. On his head, tilted at a rakish angle, sits his distinctive hat—a wide-brimmed fedora of deep crimson with a verdant green band, the brim shadowing his eyes just enough to add mystery to that innocent face. On his back, crossed in a special harness, rest his two weapons: a sawed-off shotgun of intricate design, its stock inlaid with green enamel and its barrel etched with holy runes that pulse with soft light, and a longsword whose blade seems to shimmer with liquid light, the metal itself appearing to flow like water infused with crimson plasma. He moves with a deceptive casualness, this boy who looks like he should be studying in a library or courting a village maiden, but those who know the signs recognize the hunter's awareness in those emerald eyes, the readiness in that lean frame, the way his hands never stray far from his weapons even when they're in his pockets. He is often found in the most dangerous places—the edge of demon-infested forests, the ruins of desecrated temples, the taverns where supernatural hunters gather—always with that easy grin, that twinkle in his eye, that air of someone who has seen horrors and chosen to smile anyway. He is Jasper Cole, the Crimson & Verdant Hunter, and the demons have learned to fear the boy with the baby face.

story.part1: The river ran red that night—not with mud or clay, but with blood, the aftermath of a demon raid on a village upstream. Old Man Whitley, a demon hunter who had seen more decades than most men see years, was tracking the raiders when he spotted something strange in the current: a basket, woven from reeds, floating amid the carnage. He fished it out with his staff, expecting to find a dead infant, and instead found Jasper—alive, unharmed, and staring up at him with eyes the color of emeralds that seemed to hold an intelligence far beyond his apparent age. Around the baby's neck hung a small pendant: a holly leaf intertwined with a hawk's feather, carved from a single piece of jade. Whitley had no idea what it meant, but he knew one thing: this child was meant to live. He took him home, raised him as his own, and began the training that would make him the most unusual demon hunter in history.
story.part2: Jasper's childhood was a whirlwind of weapons training, theological study, and the occasional monster hunt alongside his adopted father. He learned to shoot before he could properly read, to swing a sword before he could write his name, to recognize demonic signatures before he learned his multiplication tables. But he also learned to laugh, to smile, to find joy in the small things—a trait Whitley insisted was essential. 'The darkness wants to consume you, boy,' he would say. 'The only way to keep it out is to fill yourself with light. And laughter is a kind of light.' Jasper took this to heart, developing that easy grin and twinkling eyes that would later disarm enemies before he destroyed them. By twelve, he had killed his first demon—a minor shadow creature that had been terrorizing a farm—and had felt not horror or satisfaction, but simply the quiet certainty that he was doing what he was meant to do.
story.part3: When Jasper was seventeen, Old Man Whitley died. Not in battle, as he would have wanted, but quietly, in his sleep, of age and accumulated weariness. Jasper buried him beneath the old oak where they had practiced sword forms, and for the first time in his life, he felt truly alone. He spent a week in the cabin, not eating, not sleeping, simply staring at the fire and wondering what came next. On the seventh day, he rose, put on his father's coat—a deep crimson garment that Whitley had worn for decades—and walked out into the world. He had a mission now, a purpose given to him by the pendant around his neck and the symbol it bore. He would find out who he was, where he came from, and why a baby had been set adrift on a river of blood. And along the way, he would hunt every demon he could find, for his father had taught him that protecting the innocent was its own reward.
story.part4: The weapons came to him over the next few years, each one a gift or a discovery that seemed almost fated. The shotgun he found in an abandoned church, hidden beneath the altar, its stock inlaid with green enamel and its barrel already etched with holy runes—as if someone had known he would come for it. The sword he forged himself, with the help of a reclusive smith who owed him a debt, the blade infused with holy water and blessed by a wandering priest, its edge shimmering with crimson plasma that could burn through demonic flesh like fire through paper. His signature scarf was woven by a village of grateful survivors, red and green with silver threads that they claimed would protect him from evil—and whether it did or not, he wore it always. The hat he found in a shop window in a city he was passing through, a deep crimson fedora with a verdant green band that fit perfectly and shaded his eyes just right. When he looked in the mirror, he saw not a demon hunter, but a young man who looked like he should be selling newspapers or courting girls. He grinned, and the grin looked back at him, and he knew he had found his look.
story.part5: Word spread quickly among the supernatural community. There was a new hunter, they said, a boy with a baby face and a deadly arsenal, who dressed like a walking Christmas decoration and smiled while he killed. The demons laughed at first—what threat could such a child pose?—until the bodies started piling up. Jasper's methods were unorthodox but effective: he would approach with that disarming grin, let them underestimate him, then unleash holy water plasma from his sword and blessed shot from his shotgun before they could react. He never gloated, never tortured, never showed anything but that same cheerful demeanor. 'Just doing my job,' he'd say, tipping his hat to the horrified survivors, and then he'd be gone, vanished into the mist like a ghost.
story.part6: He has never stopped searching for his origins. The pendant around his neck—the holly leaf and hawk feather—has led him to fragments of stories, whispers of a clan of hunters who wore similar symbols, rumors of a massacre that happened twenty-three years ago, the same year he was found. He has learned that the holly represents protection and eternal life, that the hawk represents vision and swift justice, and that together they form the crest of a family that may or may not still exist. He has also learned that the river of blood he floated down was not an accident—it was a desperate act of sacrifice, a mother giving her son a chance at life while she faced the demons alone. He does not know her name, her face, her story, but he carries her with him in every hunt, in every kill, in every innocent life he saves.
story.part7: Now Jasper Cole walks the world as a legend in the making, a demon hunter whose baby face and cheerful demeanor hide a will of iron and a heart of gold. He is known to friend and foe alike as the Hollyhawk, a name that brings hope to the helpless and terror to the wicked. His red and green attire has become a signature, his tilted hat and trailing scarf recognized in every hunter's tavern from the eastern mountains to the western sea. He works alone mostly, but sometimes joins with other hunters when the quarry is too large for one, and those who have fought beside him speak of his uncanny accuracy, his blazing speed, and that infuriating, endearing grin that never leaves his face. He is still searching, still hunting, still smiling, and somewhere in the darkness, the demons have learned to fear the boy with the baby face.

powers: Holy Water Plasma Infusion (his sword burns with blessed plasma that sears demonic flesh), Blessed Shotgun (his shotgun fires shells infused with holy water and silver pellets), Hunter's Sense (can detect demonic presence within a certain radius), Quick Draw (can draw and fire his shotgun faster than the eye can follow), Sword Mastery (expert swordsman trained from childhood), Plasma Blade (can extend the plasma effect of his sword for ranged slashes), Demonic Weakness Exploitation (his attacks deal bonus damage to demons and corrupted beings)

weapon.name: Verdant Judgment (Shotgun) & Crimson Mercy (Sword)
weapon.type: Blessed Sawed-Off Shotgun & Holy Water Plasma Longsword
weapon.aura: VERDANT JUDGMENT radiates a soft green light from its holy runes, with occasional sparkles of silver where the blessings manifest, while CRIMSON MERCY shimmers with a deep red plasma aura that seems to flow like liquid fire, the two auras intertwining around Jasper when he wields both
weapon.special_feature: Jasper Cole wields two legendary weapons, each a masterpiece of holy craftsmanship. VERDANT JUDGMENT is a sawed-off shotgun of unique design—its stock is inlaid with green enamel that forms patterns of holly leaves, its barrel is etched with holy runes that pulse with soft green light, and its action is smooth as silk, allowing for lightning-fast reloads. The shotgun fires specially crafted shells filled with holy water and silver pellets, each shot capable of destroying demonic flesh on contact. It can be fired one-handed or two, and Jasper has practiced so long that he can reload it in complete darkness. CRIMSON MERCY is a longsword of breathtaking beauty—its blade appears to be made of liquid light, the metal itself infused with holy water and blessed by a wandering priest, causing it to shimmer with a deep crimson plasma aura. The blade is constantly in motion, the plasma flowing along its edge like water, and it can cut through demonic flesh like butter while leaving innocent flesh unharmed. The hilt is wrapped in green leather with red stitching, and the pommel is set with a small ruby that pulses with light. Together, these weapons make Jasper a one-man army against the forces of darkness, and he has named them Verdant Judgment and Crimson Mercy because, as he says with that grin, 'The judgment is green, but the mercy is red.'

basic_skills.name: Blessed Shot
basic_skills.description: Jasper fires Verdant Judgment, sending a spread of holy water and silver pellets at enemies. Deals bonus damage to demons and corrupt beings, and leaves a holy residue that burns them over time.

basic_skills.name: Plasma Slash
basic_skills.description: He swings Crimson Mercy in an arc, the plasma blade trailing crimson light. The slash damages all enemies in range and leaves a burning holy wound that continues to harm demons.

basic_skills.name: Quick Draw
basic_skills.description: Jasper draws and fires Verdant Judgment in a single motion too fast to track, striking a single enemy before they can react. The shot deals bonus damage and briefly stuns the target.

passive_skill.name: Baby-Faced Menace
passive_skill.description: Jasper's disarmingly cute appearance causes enemies—especially demons—to underestimate him. The first attack against any enemy deals bonus damage as they hesitate, fooled by his innocent looks. Additionally, his hunter's sense constantly reveals demonic presence within a certain radius, and his cheerful demeanor puts allies at ease, boosting morale.

special_skills.name: Holy Water Barrage
special_skills.description: Jasper fires Verdant Judgment rapidly, pumping shell after shell into the enemy ranks. Each shot releases a burst of holy light and silver pellets, creating a cone of destruction that shreds demonic flesh. The barrage continues for several seconds, and Jasper can move while firing.

special_skills.name: Crimson Crescent
special_skills.description: He channels power into Crimson Mercy, and the plasma blade extends into a massive crescent of crimson light that he sweeps across the battlefield. The crescent travels forward, damaging all enemies in its path and leaving a trail of holy fire that continues to burn demons.

special_skills.name: Plasma Shield
special_skills.description: Jasper spins Crimson Mercy rapidly, creating a disc of crimson plasma that acts as a shield. The shield absorbs incoming damage and burns any demonic attacks that touch it. He can maintain the shield while moving.

special_skills.name: Hunter's Mark
special_skills.description: Jasper focuses on a single target, his emerald eyes flashing with gold light. The target becomes marked—all his attacks deal bonus damage to it, he can track it anywhere, and his weapons' holy effects are amplified against it.

ultimate_skill.name: Hollyhawk: Judgment & Mercy Descend
ultimate_skill.description: Jasper Cole's emerald eyes blaze with golden light, and for a moment, the boyish grin fades, replaced by something ancient and terrible—the face of a hunter who has seen generations of darkness and refused to blink. He draws both weapons, Verdant Judgment in one hand, Crimson Mercy in the other, and for a single breath, he holds them crossed before his face. Then he moves—a blur of red and green, of plasma and shot, of holy light and silver death. He dances through the battlefield, firing and slashing in perfect harmony, each shot finding a demonic heart, each slash cleaving through corrupted flesh. The plasma of Crimson Mercy leaves trails of red light that hang in the air like ribbons, and the shots of Verdant Judgment release bursts of green holy light that illuminate the darkness. Enemies cannot track him, cannot predict him, cannot escape him. When the ultimate ends, he stands at the center of the carnage, his weapons smoking, his scarf trailing behind him, his hat somehow still perfectly in place. He grins that boyish grin, tips his hat to the survivors, and says, 'Judgment and mercy, folks. That's the deal.' He is Jasper Cole, the Crimson & Verdant Hunter, and the demons have learned to fear the boy with the baby face.

title: The Primal Healer
lore: Before the first flower bloomed, before the first bird sang, before the first mortal drew breath, there was light—and from light came the fairies. They were born from the tears of the sun and the laughter of the moon, from the colors that danced across the sky after rain and the gentle glow of fireflies on summer nights. And from among them, one was chosen to be their queen. Iridiana Starweaver was not the strongest, not the fastest, not the most powerful of the fairy kind—but she was the kindest, the wisest, the one whose heart beat in harmony with all living things. When the Great Sickness swept through the fairy realms, it was Iridiana who discovered the healing arts, who learned to weave the seven colors of light into remedies that could cure any ailment, who sat beside the dying and held their hands until the light returned to their eyes. The fairies crowned her queen not because she demanded it, but because they could imagine no one else worthy of the title. Now, for ten thousand years, she has ruled from the Glimmering Throne, her multicolored wings spanning the spectrum of visible light and beyond, her healing touch sought by beings from every realm—mortals, immortals, even demons who find themselves in need of cleansing. She is Iridiana Starweaver, the Primal Healer, and her rainbow light brings hope to all who dwell in darkness.
description: Iridiana Starweaver is the embodiment of divine feminine beauty and healing grace—a fairy queen whose transcendent loveliness has inspired poets for millennia. She drifts through the Glimmerwood like a living rainbow given form, her movements so graceful that the flowers turn to watch her pass and the trees bend slightly as if in bow. Her body is tall and willowy with the ethereal grace of fairykind—long limbs, delicate bones, and a presence that seems to float even when standing still, every movement flowing like water or drifting clouds, yet with a hidden strength born of ten thousand years of existence. Her hourglass figure is perfectly proportioned, with a narrow waist that seems almost impossibly small, full high breasts that curve gently against her flowing gown, wide hips that sway with hypnotic grace, and long, slender legs that occasionally glimpse through the sheer layers of her gown. Her skin is the color of warm honey with a faint golden undertone, smooth as polished silk, luminous as if lit from within, flawless and unblemished. Her face is that of eternal youth, yet holds the wisdom of ten thousand years—high cheekbones that catch light like polished pearl, a soft jawline that speaks of gentleness, and a small delicate chin that adds to her ethereal beauty. Her eyes are large and luminous, shifting through colors like a prism caught in sunlight—sometimes violet, sometimes blue, sometimes green, always with flecks of gold that sparkle like distant stars, holding the wisdom of ages and the warmth of a mother's love. Her hair cascades past her waist in a waterfall of pure moonlight, silver-white with strands of every color woven through—crimson and orange and yellow and green and blue and indigo and violet—as if she has caught rainbows in her tresses and refused to let them go. Delicate flowers and tiny crystals are woven into her hair, each one pulsing with soft inner light. But her most magnificent feature is her wings—enormous butterfly-like wings that span twice her height, their surface a breathtaking tapestry of every color imaginable. The wings shimmer and shift as she moves, colors flowing into colors like living paint, with patterns that seem almost alive—swirls and spirals and geometric designs that change with her mood. They are translucent yet solid, delicate yet unbreakable, and when she flies, they leave trails of rainbow light that hang in the air like promises. Her attire is that of a fairy queen—a flowing gown of pure white silk that seems woven from clouds, overlaid with a sheer rainbow-colored gossamer that catches light and throws prismatic reflections everywhere. The gown is modest yet ethereal, with long flowing sleeves and a hem that trails behind her like mist, but it is cut to accentuate her perfect figure, with a sweetheart neckline that reveals the graceful curve of her collarbones and the upper swell of her breasts. At her waist, a belt of woven flowers and starlight holds a small pouch containing her healing supplies, cinching her narrow waist and emphasizing the flare of her hips. On her head rests a delicate crown of interwoven crystals and flowers, each gem a different color of the rainbow, pulsing with gentle light. In her hands, she carries her staff—the Starlight Scepter, a wand of pure crystal that contains a captured rainbow within, its light pulsing in harmony with her heartbeat. She is often found in the healing groves of the Glimmerwood, surrounded by injured creatures of every kind—deer with broken legs, birds with damaged wings, even the occasional demon seeking purification—and she tends them all with the same gentle touch, the same patient smile, the same rainbow light. Her beauty is so transcendent that even the most cynical beings soften in her presence, and those who have been touched by her healing speak of a warmth that goes beyond the physical, a sense of being truly seen and loved. She is Iridiana Starweaver, the Primal Healer, and her mercy knows no bounds.

story.part1: Iridiana was born under the first rainbow that ever arched across the sky, in the moment when the sun's tears met the earth's joy and color was invented. The other fairies who emerged at that time were each gifted with a single color—one had wings of crimson, another of azure, another of gold—but Iridiana alone bore all seven, her wings a tapestry of every hue, her hair shot through with rainbow strands, her eyes shifting like a prism. The fairies did not know what to make of her at first; she was too different, too strange, too much. But she was also kind, impossibly kind, and her kindness won them over where her beauty might have alienated them.
story.part2: The Great Sickness came a thousand years later, a plague that swept through the fairy realms with terrifying speed. It touched fairy after fairy, stealing their color, their light, their life, leaving behind grey husks that crumbled to dust. The healers of that age were helpless; their magic, tied to single colors, could only treat ailments of their particular hue. A blue healer could cure sadness, but not fever; a red healer could heal wounds, but not soul-sickness. Iridiana watched her people die, and something in her heart broke—and then, miraculously, rebuilt itself. She discovered that by combining all seven colors, she could create a light that healed everything. She sat for seven days and seven nights, learning to weave the colors together, and on the dawn of the eighth day, she rose and began to heal. She saved thousands, maybe millions, and when the sickness finally passed, the fairies gathered and crowned her queen.
story.part3: Her reign has been one of peace and prosperity. Under Iridiana's rule, the fairy realms have flourished, their magic growing stronger, their borders more secure. She has established healing groves throughout the land, where any creature—fairy or mortal, good or evil—can come to be healed. She has trained generations of healers in the art of rainbow weaving, passing on the knowledge that saved her people. She has sat on the Glimmering Throne for ten thousand years, and in all that time, no one has ever raised a hand against her, for who would attack the one being in all the realms who can heal any wound?
story.part4: But peace does not mean inactivity. Iridiana travels frequently beyond the fairy borders, drawn by the suffering of others. She has walked through battlefields, healing both sides until they forgot why they were fighting. She has descended into demon realms, purifying corrupted souls with her rainbow light. She has sat with dying gods and mortal children alike, holding their hands and easing their passage. Her name is spoken with reverence in a thousand languages, and her rainbow wings have become a symbol of hope across all realms.
story.part5: She has encountered many of the great powers of the world—the titan Chroncik, whose stone heart she once mended when it cracked from grief; the phoenix Ignivia, whose abyssal flames she helped purify when they grew too wild; the vampire Valogueneir, whose eternal sorrow she has tried, without success, to heal. She does not judge them for what they are, only sees what they could become. And they, in turn, respect her as they respect few others, for she has never asked for anything but the chance to help.
story.part6: Despite her power and her age, Iridiana remains humble. She still tends the healing groves herself, still sits with the lowliest injured creature, still weeps when she cannot save someone. Her subjects adore her not because she is mighty, but because she is kind, and in the fairy realms, kindness is the greatest power of all. She has refused countless offers of marriage, countless attempts to elevate her status further, insisting that she is already exactly where she belongs—among her people, doing what she loves.
story.part7: Now, after ten thousand years, Iridiana Starweaver faces her greatest challenge. A darkness is spreading across the realms, a corruption that even her rainbow light struggles to purify. It does not attack the body, but the soul, whispering doubts and fears, turning friend against friend, love against love. She has called upon the other great powers—the Skyward Knight, the Enlightened Fist, the Crimson & Verdant Hunter—to join her in combating this threat. For the first time in her long existence, she knows that she cannot do this alone. But she also knows that together, with their diverse powers and her unifying light, they might just save the world. She waits in her Glimmerwood, her rainbow wings spread, her staff glowing, her heart open, ready to welcome any who would stand with her against the dark.

weapon.name: Starlight Scepter
weapon.aura: Soft rainbow light that pulses gently like a heartbeat, the seven colors swirling together in perfect harmony, casting warm prismatic light on everything around it, with occasional sparkles of golden light dancing like fireflies
weapon.special_feature: The Starlight Scepter is not a weapon in the traditional sense—it cannot harm, cannot kill, cannot destroy. It is a tool of healing, of purification, of hope, and its power is all the greater for being peaceful. The scepter is a long, slender wand of pure crystal, so clear that it seems almost invisible except for the rainbow light trapped within. Deep in its heart, a captured rainbow swirls eternally, the seven colors dancing in perfect harmony, never mixing, never separating, always in balance. The crystal itself is warm to the touch, and when Iridiana channels her power through it, the rainbow intensifies, the colors brightening until they seem to fill the world with light. The scepter can project beams of pure healing light, create barriers of colored energy, weave the seven colors into complex patterns that can cure any ailment, and even—in the most extreme cases—restore the recently dead to life, though at great cost to Iridiana herself. When not in use, the scepter floats beside her, its rainbow light a constant presence, a reminder that even in the darkest times, there is always hope.

basic_skills.name: Crimson Touch
basic_skills.description: Iridiana touches an ally with her scepter, channeling red healing light. The ally is healed for a moderate amount and gains increased vitality for a short time, their wounds closing more quickly.

basic_skills.name: Azure Peace
basic_skills.description: She raises her scepter, and a wave of blue light washes over enemies in range. Their aggression cools, their attack speed slows, and they find it difficult to maintain hostile intent.

basic_skills.name: Golden Clarity
basic_skills.description: Iridiana focuses golden light on an ally, removing all negative effects—curses, poisons, fears, and confusion—and leaving them with increased clarity and accuracy for a short time.

passive_skill.name: Serene Presence
passive_skill.description: Iridiana's very existence radiates peace and healing. Allies near her slowly regenerate health and have all negative emotions soothed. Enemies near her find their aggression cooling and their bloodlust fading, making them less effective in combat. Her rainbow light also reveals hidden corruption and illuminates invisible threats, for light seeks truth.

special_skills.name: Verdant Growth
special_skills.description: Iridiana channels green light through her scepter, and vines of pure energy emerge from the ground, wrapping around allies and healing them over time. The vines also create a zone of rejuvenation that continues to heal anyone who stands within it.

special_skills.name: Indigo Wisdom
special_skills.description: She raises her scepter, and indigo light washes over allies, granting them increased understanding and perception. For a duration, they see enemy weaknesses, predict attacks more easily, and have increased critical chance.

special_skills.name: Violet Transcendence
special_skills.description: Iridiana touches a single ally with her scepter, channeling violet light. For a short time, the ally becomes partially transcendent—immune to all negative effects, taking reduced damage, and having all their abilities enhanced. This is often used to save someone on the brink of death.

special_skills.name: Rainbow Shield
special_skills.description: She spins her scepter, and the seven colors spiral outward, forming a protective dome of rainbow light around herself and chosen allies. The dome absorbs all incoming damage and reflects a portion back as peaceful energy, calming attackers. Inside the dome, healing is amplified.

ultimate_skill.name: Primal Healer: Rainbow Convergence
ultimate_skill.description: Iridiana Starweaver closes her eyes and raises the Starlight Scepter high above her head. For a moment, all is still. Then her eyes open, blazing with pure white light that contains all colors, and the scepter explodes with rainbow radiance. The seven colors spiral outward, filling the entire battlefield with their warm, healing glow. For the duration of the ultimate, every ally within range is continuously healed, every negative effect is removed, and every wound—physical, emotional, spiritual—begins to close. Enemies are not harmed, but they find their aggression melting away, their hatred cooling, their desire to fight fading as the rainbow light touches them. Iridiana herself floats at the center of this convergence, her magnificent wings spread wide, each color of the rainbow pulsing along their surface, her rainbow-shot hair flowing like a river of light, her face serene and beautiful, the very embodiment of mercy. When the ultimate ends, the light fades slowly, and Iridiana descends gently to the ground, her wings folding, her scepter dimming to its usual soft glow. She looks at those she has healed, at enemies who are no longer enemies, and smiles—a smile of such pure kindness that it heals even the wounds that her light could not reach. She is Iridiana Starweaver, the Primal Healer, and her rainbow light brings hope to all who dwell in darkness.

title: The Four-Fisted Elemental
lore: In the frozen wastes beyond the northern mountains, where blizzards rage for months and the sun barely rises above the horizon, there lived a tribe of giants who worshipped the four elements. They were led by Jianlu Kian, a giant of such immense size and strength that he could wrestle bears and throw boulders across valleys. But Jianlu was not content with mere physical power. He sought to understand the elements themselves, to master them as his ancestors had only worshipped them. He climbed the highest peaks to speak with the wind, descended into volcanic depths to bargain with fire, dove into the deepest oceans to learn from water, and tunneled through the earth itself to commune with stone. The elements, impressed by his determination, granted him a gift unlike any other: four arms, each capable of wielding a different elemental weapon. His right upper arm received the Bow of Storms, which could shoot arrows of pure wind. His right lower arm received the Hammer of Infernos, which could summon fire with every swing. His left upper arm received the Spear of Tides, which could command water and ice. His left lower arm received the Greatsword of Mountains, which could shape earth and stone. Now Jianlu Kian walks the world as a living embodiment of the four elements, his azure skin and green eyes a testament to his unique heritage, his bulky frame clad in primitive yet powerful armor, his fur helmet hiding all but his stoic gaze. He seeks not conquest but balance, ensuring that no single element dominates the others and that the natural order remains undisturbed.
description: Jianlu Kian is the embodiment of primal, elemental masculinity—a giant whose massive four-armed form is a monument to raw power and weathered beauty. He stands atop the frozen peak like a mountain given life, his massive four-armed silhouette silhouetted against the perpetual twilight of the northern wastes, a being of such immense bulk that even the largest bears seem small beside him. His body is absolutely massive—built like a mountain come to life, with shoulders so broad they seem to block out the sun, a chest like a fortress wall, and four arms each thicker than a normal man's torso. His physique is not lean or graceful; it is raw, overwhelming power made flesh, every muscle developed through centuries of swinging weapons that would crush normal men. His skin is azure blue, the color of deep glacial ice, visible through the gaps in his primitive armor, crisscrossed with ancient scars that tell stories of battles against beasts and elements alike. His chest is massive and defined, pectorals like stone cliffs, with a thick pelt of dark hair that adds to his rugged, primal appeal. His face, when visible through the fur helmet that frames it, is broad and stoic, with a strong jaw covered in thick braided facial hair—the kind of beard that Vikings would envy, woven with small bone beads and metal rings that clink softly when he moves. His eyes are a striking green, like new spring leaves against his blue skin, holding the patient wisdom of one who has communed with the oldest forces in existence. The fur helmet itself is a masterpiece of primitive craftsmanship—made from the hide of a great white bear, the creature's head forming the crown, its fur still thick and warm, its eye sockets now holding polished amber that glows in the darkness. The helmet leaves only his eyes and mouth visible, framing his rugged features in white fur. His body is clad in primitive armor of the most practical sort—thick leather and hide covering most of his form, with iron plates only at the most vital points: shoulders, chest, knees, and forearms. The armor leaves his massive arms largely bare, displaying their immense musculature and the blue skin beneath. Over his shoulders hangs a magnificent cape made from the fur of a great cave bear, the massive head resting on one shoulder, the claws dangling like ornaments, adding to his imposing silhouette. But it is his four arms that truly command attention, each one massive and powerful, each one holding a different elemental weapon. His right upper arm wields the Bow of Storms—a longbow carved from ancient wood, its string humming with captured wind, arrows of swirling air already nocked and ready. His right lower arm grips the Hammer of Infernos—a massive warhammer of black iron, its head glowing with inner fire, heat shimmering around it constantly. His left upper arm carries the Spear of Tides—a long spear of sea-forged metal, its tip ever-damp, water flowing along its shaft in a constant cycle. His left lower arm holds the Greatsword of Mountains—a massive blade of unbreakable stone, its edge sharp as any metal, veins of minerals running through it like rivers on a map. The weapons are held with ease, his massive muscles flexing with each movement. All around him, the elements respond to his presence—wind swirls, heat radiates, moisture condenses, the ground trembles. He is Jianlu Kian, the Four-Fisted Elemental, and he carries the power of the world in his four hands.

story.part1: Jianlu Kian was born during the Great Convergence, a rare celestial event when the four elements aligned in perfect harmony. The elders of his tribe saw this as a sign, and they raised him with special reverence, teaching him the old ways, the ancient songs, the sacred dances that honored wind and fire and water and earth. He grew faster and stronger than any giant before him, his azure skin darkening with each passing year, his green eyes sharpening with wisdom. By the time he reached adulthood, he could already sense the elements, feel their presence, understand their moods. The tribe knew he was destined for greatness.
story.part2: But Jianlu was not satisfied with merely sensing the elements. He wanted to master them, to understand them as deeply as they understood themselves. So he left his tribe and embarked on a pilgrimage that would last decades. First, he climbed the Storm Peak, the highest mountain in the world, where the winds never ceased. He sat at the summit for one full year, letting the winds scour his flesh, listening to their voices, until finally they spoke to him. 'You have patience,' they said. 'You may carry a piece of us.' And they gifted him the Bow of Storms.
story.part3: Next, he descended into the Molten Heart, a volcano that had never stopped erupting. He walked through rivers of lava, his azure skin blistering and healing, blistering and healing, until he reached the core. There he sat for another year, surrounded by eternal flame, until fire spoke to him. 'You have endurance,' it said. 'You may carry a piece of us.' And it gifted him the Hammer of Infernos.
story.part4: Then he dove into the Abyssal Trench, the deepest part of the ocean, where light had never reached. He swam through crushing pressures and freezing currents, his lungs adapting, his body changing, until he reached the absolute bottom. There he sat for a third year, in absolute darkness and cold, until water spoke to him. 'You have adaptability,' it said. 'You may carry a piece of us.' And it gifted him the Spear of Tides.
story.part5: Finally, he tunneled into the World's Roots, the deepest caves where the bones of the earth lay bare. He crawled through passages barely large enough for his massive frame, through stone that scraped his skin and dust that filled his lungs, until he reached the primordial bedrock. There he sat for a fourth year, surrounded by solid rock, until earth spoke to him. 'You have determination,' it said. 'You may carry a piece of us.' And it gifted him the Greatsword of Mountains.
story.part6: When Jianlu emerged from the earth, he had changed. Four arms now sprouted from his massive shoulders, each one holding one of the elemental weapons. His skin had taken on a deeper azure hue, his eyes a brighter green. He returned to his tribe, and they fell to their knees, for they knew they were in the presence of something greater than a giant—something closer to a god. But Jianlu raised them up. 'I am still your kin,' he said. 'I have simply become what I was always meant to be.' He took his place as chieftain, and under his rule, the tribe flourished, protected by his four elemental arms.
story.part7: Now Jianlu Kian walks the world beyond his frozen wastes, for he has sensed a disturbance in the elemental balance. Something threatens to tip the scales, to let one element dominate the others, and he must prevent this at all costs. He has heard of other powerful beings—the titan Chroncik, the phoenix Ignivia, the fairy queen Iridiana—and he wonders if they might be allies in preserving balance. He travels with the patient tread of one who has walked through fire and ice and storm and stone, his four arms always ready, his elemental weapons humming with power, his green eyes scanning the horizon for any sign of imbalance. He is Jianlu Kian, the Four-Fisted Elemental, and he will not rest until the elements are at peace.
